lines.text: How does an app like YouTube or TikTok know exactly what video you want to watch before you even search for it?
It doesn't just look at what videos you like; it tracks your behavior down to the millisecond.
Machine learning models measure watch time, how fast you scroll, rewatches, and where you pause.
It groups your viewing patterns with millions of similar users into high-dimensional mathematical clusters.
Candidate generation algorithms filter hundreds of thousands of candidate videos down to a top hundred.
A deep ranking neural network scores each video on the probability that you will finish and share it.
The algorithm doesn't read your mind; it simply predicts your habits with superhuman precision.
